subject: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechco.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Happy to adjust anything I misunderstood.

Key pain points you described:
- Recent production incidents (Mar 22 outage + Mar 30 latency spikes) that caused request errors and timeouts during peak trading windows.
- Autoscaling lag and large KV-cache cold-starts leading to 30-40% error amplification during bursts.
- No rapid cross-region failover in current stack; manual DNS/traffic cutover required.
- Lack of detailed per-request audit logs and retention limits (need 12mo+ for compliance).

Current stack (as discussed):
- Frontend routing: ALB -> internal API layer -> in-house inference cluster (Kubernetes + Triton) running an open LLM.
- Hosting: AWS us-west-2 primary, limited DR in eu-west-1 but not automated.
- Observability: basic dashboards, limited token-level cost breakdowns.

Success criteria you called out:
- Error rate < 0.1% during peak; automatic degradation vs full fail (keep service responsive).
- p95 latency target < 500ms for short responses; < 2s for long generations.
- Cross-region failover under 30s for traffic-critical endpoints.
- One-year audit log retention + export capability for compliance.

Potential Redwood approaches we discussed (high level):
- Multi-tier graceful degradation: prefix/KV caching, reduced context fallback, and model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model) to preserve availability rather than returning errors.
- Automated cross-region routing + health-based failover with warm replicas in eu-west-1 to meet the 30s objective.
- Dedicated capacity option for predictable throughput during market peaks and guaranteed SLOs (99.9%+ availability for committed pools).
- Circuit breakers, rate-limited queueing, and progressive backpressure to prevent cascading failures during bursts.
- Token-level tracing and audit logs with configurable retention (we can support 12+ months with archive to your S3/KMS).

Attachments & links included: short questionnaire on reliability (reliability-questions.docx) and the meeting recording (Drive link).

Next steps (proposed):
1) You send the internal incident report and any SLO/SLA docs you already have (Elena — you mentioned a March incident report).
2) We schedule a technical deep dive with our Solutions Engineer to map failover design and the KV-cache strategy (proposed: Tues Apr 6, 10:00 PT).
3) Redwood to send a PoC SOW for a 4–6 week test: warm replicas in eu-west-1, model-variant fallback, dedicated small reserved pool during peak windows.
4) We'll include an initial cost/throughput estimate and draft SLAs for the PoC.

If that all matches your expectations, I'll schedule the deep dive and get the PoC SOW over to you.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: reliability-questions.docx (questions on incident cadence, traffic profile, KV cache TTLs)
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation

Thanks Marissa — this is a great summary and yes, aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and additional details from our side:

Incident history (quick):
- Mar 22 (02:15–04:10 UTC): Partial outage — internal autoscaler failed to spin up nodes quickly enough; caused 2 hours of elevated errors for async endpoints.
- Mar 30 (14:40–15:05 UTC): Short burst-induced latency spike; traced to large KV cache evictions after a config change and a hot prefix.
- We did not have a clean cross-region failover; manual ops required to route traffic to eu-west-1 and rehydrate caches.

Our prioritized success criteria:
- Error rates under 0.1% in peak windows (this is non-negotiable for certain trading flows).
- p95 < 500ms on synchronous endpoints.
- Warm cross-region failover within 30s for critical routes.
- Auditable logs exported to our S3 for 12 months; exports must be signed (KMS).

Questions for Redwood:
1) How fast can a quantized fallback model spin up from warm cold storage? What impact on latency at p95?
2) Can you support incremental KV cache rehydration so we avoid full cold-cache storms?
3) Would Dedicated pools with burst capacity remove the autoscaling lag we observed?

I've attached our internal incident report for March (redacted). Happy to discuss further in the technical deep-dive.

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
elena.rossi@fintechco.com

Attachment: fintechco-incident-report-march2026.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechco.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fintechco.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — Reliability & graceful degradation

Elena — thanks for the incident details, very helpful. Short answers to your questions below and proposed concrete next steps. We'll cover the details in the deep-dive.

1) Quantized fallback spin-up:
- We can keep a small hot pool of the quantized variant (4-bit) in each region; warm pool means <1s cold-start for routing, p95 impact typically +50–150ms depending on generation length. If you prefer no spin-up at all, we can provision a minimal always-warm pool (cost tradeoff).

2) Incremental KV rehydration:
- Yes — Redwood supports incremental/priority key rehydration. We can seed hot-prefixes based on recent traffic and stream rehydration in background to avoid mass evictions.

3) Dedicated pools and autoscaling lag:
- Dedicated reserved pools eliminate the cluster-level autoscaling step for capacity inside the pool. You still have autoscaling for burst beyond the reserved commit, but we can configure burst capacity and pre-warm windows around known market events (cron-based).

Proposed PoC (deliverables & timeline):
- 4–6 week PoC: warm quantized replicas in eu-west-1, cross-region health-based failover configured, incremental KV rehydration enabled for top prefixes, token-level tracing with 12mo export to your S3.
- SLA targets for PoC: availability objective 99.9% for committed routes; we'll provide monitoring and alerting.
- PoC SOW attached. Estimated start week of Apr 12 if we sign the SOW by Apr 9.

I'll have Jonas and Dev draft the technical SOW and routing design diagrams. Can we confirm the deep-dive time: Tue Apr 6, 10:00 PT?

Links: PoC SOW (attached) + DocuSign for signature: https://www.docusign.com/mock/FTCO-PoC
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/FTCO-2026-0421

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Marissa Cole
